title: Five Teams, Six Points, and the Tightest MLC Race American Cricket Has Ever Seen
excerpt: MI New York's five-run win over Seattle has left five of six franchises level on points with the playoffs a fortnight away. For NRIs across America, the sport they grew up with has never felt closer.
body:
Five teams. Six points each. Net run rate as thin as a late-order edge. This is Major League Cricket's third season, and it has never been this close.

MI New York's five-run win over the Seattle Orcas in Redmond on Wednesday night — Romario Shepherd earning the Player of the Match award for his all-round effort — tightened the table into something that looks more like a traffic jam than a cricket standings. Five of the six MLC franchises are now level on six points, separated only by that most fickle of arbiters: net run rate.

## The table as it stands

San Francisco Unicorns sit at the top with a net run rate of +0.489, built largely on the back of commanding wins and Ashwin's midseason arrival that has steadied both their spin attack and their batting order. MI New York, having won three of their five completed games, are second on +0.259. The Seattle Orcas (+0.199), Texas Super Kings (+0.033) and Washington Freedom (−0.888) round out the five-way tie. Only the Los Angeles Knight Riders, Shah Rukh Khan's franchise that just made history by opening the first franchise-owned cricket stadium in Pomona, are adrift on four points from five matches — though with games in hand, they remain very much alive.

## Why this matters for the diaspora

The tight race means high-stakes matches across American cities where Indian communities are densest. This week alone, games were played or are scheduled in Redmond (Washington state, home to Microsoft and a vast Indian tech workforce), Grand Prairie (the Dallas–Fort Worth corridor), Pomona (Southern California), and Fairfax (the Virginia suburb that is practically an extension of the Indian embassy belt). For NRIs who grew up arguing about points tables in the IPL, the conversation has arrived in their backyards — literally.

> **"MI New York, having won three of their five completed games, are second on +0.259."**

## Wednesday's match in Redmond

Seattle won the toss and chose to bowl, but MI New York posted 132 for 8 in their 20 overs — modest, but enough. The Orcas' chase stalled repeatedly. Marcus Stoinis top-scored with 36 off 31 balls, and Shehan Jayasuriya added 19, but Seattle lost wickets at regular intervals and finished on 127 for 9. Shepherd's discipline with the ball, combined with his handy lower-order runs, proved the difference.

It was Seattle's fourth defeat in seven completed matches, and it exposed a recurring issue: the Orcas have the star power — Stoinis, Shimron Hetmyer, Dasun Shanaka — but have struggled to string together a complete batting performance when it counts.

## The playoff picture

Four of the six teams will qualify for the playoffs, which begin on July 16 at the Oakland Coliseum. With every team having between three and five games remaining, any result can rearrange the top four. The only certainty right now is that there is no certainty.

The San Francisco Unicorns, bolstered by Ashwin's off-spin and a steady top order led by captain Matthew Short, are best placed on net run rate. But their remaining schedule includes MI New York twice and the Knight Riders — three matches against sides that have everything to play for.

MI New York face the Knight Riders on the Fourth of July in Pomona, a match that could be one of the most consequential in the league's short history. Nicholas Pooran's side have been efficient rather than explosive — and in a tight league, efficiency might be exactly what gets you through.

## What's next

Friday, July 4: Los Angeles Knight Riders vs MI New York at Knight Riders Cricket Ground, Pomona.

Saturday, July 5: Seattle Orcas vs Texas Super Kings at Marymoor Park, Redmond.

Sunday, July 6: San Francisco Unicorns vs MI New York at AirHogs Stadium, Grand Prairie.

Three matches, three potential table reshuffles. If you are anywhere near a ground, the admission is cheap, the cricket is fast, and the stakes have never been higher.
